QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_34

question.text: A Section 8 Company under the Companies Act 2013 is defined by which of the following key features?

answer.text: Its objective is promotion of commerce, art, science, research, education, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any such other object; it applies its profits in promoting its objectives; and it prohibits payment of any dividend to its members.
It must have minimum 100 members and paid-up capital of Rs 5 crore.
It must be a wholly-owned subsidiary of a listed company.
It pays dividends only out of reserves, not current profits.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Box 2.2 on p.57 of the workbook, the Companies Act defines a Section 8 company as one whose objective is the promotion of commerce, art, science, research, education, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any such other object; it applies its profits in promoting these objectives; and it prohibits payment of any dividend to its members. The Trap: Option B invents capital/member thresholds. Option C invents a subsidiary-only restriction. Option D muddles with conventional company dividend rules. Note: The three-part Section 8 definition (eligible objects + application of profits to objects + dividend prohibition) on p.57 is the operative source.
